rationales: Carbon-14 is primarily used for dating and tracing, not internal cancer treatment.
Phosphorus-32 is used as a radiotherapeutic isotope within the body.
Cobalt-60 is mainly used for external radiation therapy.
Strontium-90 is not the isotope typically used for this purpose.
Compounds are chemically combined and cannot be separated by physical means.
Radicals are groups of atoms or ions, not mixtures separable by physical means.
Elements cannot be broken into simpler substances by physical means.
Mixtures can be separated by physical methods such as filtration or distillation.
A triple covalent bond consists of three shared pairs, or six electrons.
Four electrons form two shared pairs, corresponding to a double bond.
Three electrons cannot make the three shared pairs in a triple bond.
Eight electrons are not involved in a single triple bond.
A metal–nonmetal bond is generally formed by electron transfer, not covalent sharing.
Electron transfer between a metal and a nonmetal typically forms an ionic bond.
Coordinate covalent bonds involve a shared pair donated by one atom, which is not the expected bond here.
Metallic bonding occurs among metal atoms, not between a metal and a nonmetal.
Mass per 100 cm³ is not the definition of % m/v.
Mass per 100 g of solution is the definition of % m/m.
Volume of solute per 100 cm³ of solution is the definition of % v/v.
Volume per 100 g of solution is not the stated concentration basis.
Forming water is not an acid–base reaction.
Hydrogen is oxidized and oxygen is reduced, so the reaction is redox.
Hydrogen and oxygen combine to form water rather than one substance decomposing.
No acid and base are neutralizing one another to form water and a salt.
Some metals form unipositive ions, such as sodium ions.
Some metals form dipositive ions, such as magnesium ions.
Some metals form tripositive ions, such as aluminium ions.
Metals can form unipositive, dipositive, and tripositive ions.
Sodium chloride is soluble in water.
Potassium chloride is soluble in water.
Calcium chloride is soluble in water.
Benzene, C₆H₆, is nonpolar and does not dissolve appreciably in water.
Na is the symbol for sodium.
Ca is the symbol for calcium.
Ag is the symbol for silver.
Si is the symbol for silicon.
Canal rays consist of positively charged ions.
Canal rays are not negatively charged.
Canal rays carry charge rather than being neutral.
Canal rays carry full positive charge, not partial negative charge.
Periods are the horizontal rows of the modern periodic table.
Groups are the vertical columns of the modern periodic table.
Noble gases are a family of elements, not the name for all vertical columns.
Transition elements are a category of elements, not the name for vertical columns.
Transfer of electrons between atoms forms an ionic bond.
Covalent bonds form by sharing electrons.
Metallic bonds involve delocalized electrons among metal atoms.
Coordinate covalent bonds form when one atom donates a shared electron pair.
Hydrogen has the lowest molar mass among these gases and diffuses fastest.
Helium diffuses quickly but more slowly than hydrogen.
Fluorine is much heavier than hydrogen and diffuses more slowly.
Chlorine is heavier than hydrogen and diffuses more slowly.
A 2 M solution has the greatest solute concentration and, for equal solution volumes, less water.
A 1 M solution is more concentrated than the 0.5 M and 0.25 M solutions.
A 0.5 M solution is more concentrated than the 0.25 M solution.
A 0.25 M solution has the lowest solute concentration and thus contains the most water for equal solution volumes.
Liquids are generally about 1000 times denser than gases, not 100 times.
Liquids are generally about 1000 times denser than gases.
A factor of 10000 is too large for the usual comparison of liquid and gas densities.
A factor of 100000 is too large for the usual comparison of liquid and gas densities.
